content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":5,"description_fidelity":8,"readability_1x":6,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":7,"appeal":6},"score":59,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The sprite appears roughly 26x27 pixels, substantially larger and more sprawling than the intended 16x16 to 20x20 enemy.","At 1x, the blue cap, central black mass, eyes, and tentacles compete rather than forming one immediate squid silhouette.","The upper-right black shape is oversized and ambiguous; it reads as a separate appendage or hole instead of part of the robot body.","Several outline areas are 2-3 pixels thick, especially around the cap, eye assembly, and lower-right body, unlike the controlled 1-pixel Capcom contouring.","The lower tentacles contain busy cyan-blue stair-steps and small clusters that become visual noise at true size.","The eyes are readable but oversized and rigidly rectangular, giving a fan-sprite expression rather than the compact mechanical character design typical of MM2/MM3.","The long horizontal black extension on the right looks accidental and weakens the silhouette.","The frame does not visually suggest an armed or flashing mine state; there is no red eye accent in this presentation."],"fixes":["Compress the design to about 18x18 or 20x20 pixels and keep all tentacles inside a tighter, rounded silhouette.","Reduce the cap to a simpler dome with a continuous 1-pixel black contour and one compact cyan highlight cluster.","Shrink and clarify the upper-right black mass, integrating it as a small face joint or body shadow rather than a large void.","Use two smaller white eye blocks with single-pixel pupils; reserve red replacement pixels for the warning animation frame.","Remove the rightward black bar and close the body contour cleanly behind the eyes.","Simplify the tentacles into three bold prongs: a gathered pose and a clearly extended thrust pose, with fewer internal blue/cyan steps.","Replace thick outline patches with deliberate 1-pixel contours, allowing thickness only where black also serves as interior separation.","Limit each local 8x8 region to black, blue, cyan or white plus transparency, avoiding unnecessary overlap of all four visible colors."]}
